walkthroughs.body_html:
Statistical Hypothesis Testing — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Statistical Hypothesis Testing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Statistical Hypothesis Testing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the derivative of (3x + 1)^2 with respect to x?
options: 6(3x + 1) — by the chain rule, multiplying by the derivative of the inside (3).
The derivative is 2(3x + 1) — applying the power rule without the chain rule.
The derivative is 9x^2 + 6x + 1 by leaving it as it is.
6, by multiplying -3 by 2.
9, because squaring a negative number always gives a positive.
The derivative is 9x^2 + 6x + 1 by leaving it as it is.
-9 — without brackets, the exponent applies only to the 3, then the negative is applied: -(3^2) = -9.
6, by multiplying -3 by 2.

mcqs.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. What is the relationship between co-interior (allied) angles?
options: They add up to 360 degrees because they make a full turn.
6, by multiplying -3 by 2.
They add up to 180 degrees.
They are equal to each other, like alternate angles.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “P-value”?
options: Set of observed values for which H₀ is rejected. Found from significance level and distribution under H₀.
Probability, under H₀, of observing data as extreme or more extreme than the observed. Reject H₀ if p < α.
α (often 5%, 1%). Probability of rejecting H₀ when it is true (Type I error).
One-tailed: alternative specifies direction (e.g., p > 0.5). Two-tailed: any difference (p ≠ 0.5). Affects critical region.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Significance level”?
options: Set of observed values for which H₀ is rejected. Found from significance level and distribution under H₀.
Type I: reject true H₀ (rate = α). Type II: fail to reject false H₀ (rate β). Power = 1 − β.
One-tailed: alternative specifies direction (e.g., p > 0.5). Two-tailed: any difference (p ≠ 0.5). Affects critical region.
α (often 5%, 1%). Probability of rejecting H₀ when it is true (Type I error).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Type I & Type II errors”?
options: H₀ is the default (e.g., p = 0.5). H₁ is what we test against (one-tailed or two-tailed). Decide based on evidence.
Type I: reject true H₀ (rate = α). Type II: fail to reject false H₀ (rate β). Power = 1 − β.
Set of observed values for which H₀ is rejected. Found from significance level and distribution under H₀.
Probability, under H₀, of observing data as extreme or more extreme than the observed. Reject H₀ if p < α.
